Drafts: a 65%-rule take on RE + BTC, a one-number question, and a Philly leverage warning.

drafts.draft_en:
Everyone's asking if you should add Bitcoin to real estate.

My question is simpler: does the house work without it?

In Philly I only buy when purchase plus repairs is at or under 65% of after-repair value.

If a deal needs a price prediction to work, it isn't a deal.
drafts.pattern: Rides the RE + BTC hook (Cardone 1100 BTC question at 24.2k; 'Real Estate + Bitcoin' at 21.0k) and brings it back to Bar's 65% all-in rule. No price calls, no promised returns.
drafts.video_tip: Talking head, 15s. Hold up a phone with a BTC chart, put it face-down, then point at a Philly rowhome. Say 'Does the house work without it?' Put '65% of ARV' on screen.

drafts.draft_en: What's the one number you check before you make an offer on a house?
drafts.pattern: One-line question format (Cardone 'What's changed about the company?' at 228.1k with 851 replies; TheREDevGUY's mortgage question at 341.8k). Short, open, easy to answer.
drafts.video_tip: Skip video; post as text. If you film it, do 6s: you on a Philly stoop, question on screen, end with 'Drop yours below.'

drafts.draft_en:
Charlie Munger said smart people go broke 3 ways: liquor, ladies, and leverage.

In real estate, it's almost always the third.

Debt feels fine on the way up. On the way down, only your buy price protects you.

Buy right. Keep reserves. Build slowly. That's how a legacy lasts.
